# A made-up case for tests/test_law.rex, under CMA 1990 s.1 (E.W.) with the CPS guidance: no real person,
# place or system.  Written by Claude (Opus 5.5), 2026-10-29.  step | element | SUPPORT or REBUT | tier | binding | text
1 | 1 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | ACCOUNT_ACT | the server log of S shows the account p.user ran a command at 02:14
1 | 1 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | REQUEST_TO_ANOTHER | an e-mail from P asks the operator Q to pull the payroll report from S
2 | 1 | SUPPORT | STYLOMETRIC | PERSON_ACT | the command history reads like the way P types
3 | 1 | SUPPORT | PROVENANCE | PERSON_ACT | the login at 02:14 was approved by the hardware key registered to P, signature verified
4 | 2 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | INTENT | the command at 02:14 was cat payroll.csv: it reads a data file
5 | 3 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | AUTHORITY | a manager writes that P should not have looked at payroll
5 | 3 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | DEFINED_LIMITS | the written access list for P's role, issued to P, does not include server S
6 | 4 | SUPPORT | TESTIMONY | KNOWLEDGE | a colleague says P was told not to use server S
6 | 4 | REBUT | TESTIMONY | KNOWLEDGE | P says he believed his role had access to server S
6 | 4 | SUPPORT | TESTIMONY | RECKLESSNESS | a colleague says P must have guessed it might be off limits
7 | 4 | SUPPORT | DOCUMENTARY | KNOWLEDGE | an e-mail from the administrator to P, two days before, refusing access to server S, with P's read receipt
